known-gaps.description: pyflakes needs Python, which this toolchain does not require of the host, so run: scripts with shell: python are not linted for Python errors.
The ShellCheck family accepts any code from SC1000 to SC3999, including one ShellCheck never emits, because the set of codes is generated from the pinned source by the currency phase (phase 8).
A step whose runs-on: is an expression that resolves to a Windows runner is checked as bash, so a PowerShell script there can draw false ShellCheck findings; give the step an explicit shell: pwsh.

The zizmor lane runs offline and at zizmor's regular persona. Its online audits (impostor-commit, known-vulnerable-actions, ref-confusion, ref-version-mismatch, stale-action-refs), forbidden-uses, which needs a policy, and insecure-url-scheme, which reads only a pre-commit configuration that is not collected, have an identifier and a page but are not run, and every run of the lane names each of them on the diagnostic stream with its reason. The pedantic and auditor audits are shown by the rule harness (`rule`) but not by `check`, until the project record can enable them.

actionlint's potentially-untrusted messages of its expression kind and zizmor's template-injection report the same hazard, so one expression can carry two identifiers and need two exceptions. The actionlint messages are kept because zizmor's regular persona, which check runs, does not report a fromJSON of an untrusted input; they are dropped once the default persona is decided.

actionlint's credentials kind is dropped in favour of zizmor's hardcoded-container-credentials, which does not report a container or service password that is a secret followed by a literal expression (${{ secrets.A }}${{ 'x' }}) or an empty one (null, ~).

`check` runs the actionlint lane in a child process with a time limit, so a workflow that crashes its parser or never finishes is exit 4; but the `rule` harness still runs actionlint inside its own process, so a workflow built to recurse without bound (a million nested parentheses) ends `rule` with the Go runtime's own exit code 2, and one built to be slow runs there without a time bound.

actionsqaci.templateDrift compares a copy with its source byte for byte. The design's identical-except mode, which lets a copy differ in named YAML keys, is not built, because the key-path syntax is not specified; a record that tries to state it is refused, so nothing is silently ignored.

actionsqaci.requiredChecks compares the record's required contexts with the workflows in the repository, offline. The comparison with the branch protection and rulesets a repository actually has is made only under `check --online`, with a token that can read branch protection (the token an Actions run gets by default cannot), so a run without it does not find a protection that requires a context the record does not list, or omits one it does. An app-supplied context is compared by name only. A job that calls a reusable workflow is accepted for any context under its name, because the called workflow is not read.

The SARIF log gives each rule's helpUri as its page on the default branch, where the design puts it at the release tag, because the program has no release version to name a tag with until the distribution phase (phase 7). The log names no driver version either.

A workflow file holding a second YAML document is analysed on its first document only, and the second is not read; whether GitHub accepts such a file is not confirmed, so it stays a gap until the lint-coverage check (phase 6) decides it.
That actions-qa-ci is the Detector and zizmor and actionlint are bundled rule backends is a reading of toolchain 4.1 the specification does not spell out; it stands until the Owner confirms it.
